events.title: US military operation topples Maduro, sets hemispheric tone
events.detail: US forces launched a military assault on Venezuela, capturing President Nicolás Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores and extraditing them to New York. The operation, framed by Washington as a counter-narco-terrorism action, left more than 100 dead including civilians, and is widely read as the opening move of the 'Trump Corollary' to the Monroe Doctrine that the Shield of the Americas would later formalize.
events.confidenceReason: US government confirms the operation and Maduro's capture; casualty figures (100+) come from secondary reporting and are contested by human rights monitors.

events.title: Colombia reinforces Venezuela border after US strike
events.detail: Colombia deployed additional troops to its border with Venezuela in the immediate aftermath of the US operation against Maduro, citing instability and possible cross-border spillover from Venezuelan security forces and armed groups.

events.title: Three boat strikes kill 11 in Pacific and Caribbean
events.detail: US Southern Command carried out three lethal strikes on small vessels in the eastern Pacific and Caribbean in a single day, killing 11 people SOUTHCOM said were engaged in narcotics smuggling. The strikes were part of Operation Southern Spear, the kinetic campaign that would become the operational backbone of the coalition founded weeks later; the campaign has killed at least 190 people in more than 50 strikes since September 2025.
events.confidenceReason: SOUTHCOM confirms strikes and target identification as traffickers; independent verification of each vessel's cargo/intent is not possible.

events.title: Joint Security Declaration signed at SOUTHCOM headquarters
events.detail: Two days ahead of the leaders' summit, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, Homeland Security Adviser Stephen Miller, and SOUTHCOM commander Gen. Francis Donovan met regional defense ministers and military chiefs at SOUTHCOM headquarters in Doral to finalize the Joint Security Declaration underpinning the coalition.

events.title: Trump hosts founding summit, 17 nations sign Doral Charter
events.detail: President Trump convened Western Hemisphere leaders at Trump National Doral in Miami on 7 March 2026. Twelve heads of state attended in person (Argentina, Bolivia, Costa Rica, Dominican Republic, Ecuador, El Salvador, Guyana, Honduras, Panama, Paraguay, Trinidad and Tobago, and the US), with six more nations signing on (Bahamas, Belize, Chile, Guatemala, Jamaica, Peru), for 17 initial signatories to the Doral Charter. The summit launched both the diplomatic 'Shield of the Americas' forum and its operational military arm, the Americas Counter Cartel Coalition (A3C), with the motto 'We do bad things to bad people.' Kristi Noem was named special envoy.

events.title: Trump signs minerals deal alongside Chile's Kast at summit
events.detail: On the sidelines of the founding summit, Trump signed a critical-minerals cooperation agreement with newly inaugurated Chilean President José Antonio Kast, folding economic cooperation into the coalition's security-first agenda.

events.title: Díaz-Canel calls summit 'neocolonial'; Trump warns Cuba is 'at the end of the line'
events.detail: Cuban President Miguel Díaz-Canel denounced the Doral summit as 'small,' 'reactionary,' and 'neocolonial,' accusing Washington of endorsing lethal force against sovereign governments' internal affairs. Trump responded at the summit by warning that Cuba's government was 'at the end of the line,' escalating rhetoric against Havana.

events.title: Region's three largest economies absent from founding summit
events.detail: Mexico, Brazil and Colombia — the hemisphere's three largest economies, all under left-leaning governments at the time — were not part of the founding signatories. Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum said she had rejected a US offer to send troops into Mexico against cartels, insisting Mexico would act on its own with only intelligence-sharing cooperation with Washington.

events.title: Bahamas, Belize, Guatemala, Jamaica and Chile formalize accession
events.detail: In the weeks following the founding summit, the Bahamas, Belize, Guatemala, Jamaica and Chile (under President José Antonio Kast) completed formal accession to the coalition, bringing total membership toward 18 as coordination mechanisms under SOUTHCOM's Joint Interagency Task Force-South began to stand up.

events.title: US forces strike suspected narco boat in eastern Pacific
events.detail: US forces conducted another lethal strike on a vessel suspected of drug trafficking in the eastern Pacific, part of the continuing Southern Spear campaign that member states cite as evidence of coalition resolve and critics cite as evidence of due-process violations.

events.title: Caribbean and eastern Pacific strikes kill 5
events.detail: US forces killed five people in separate strikes on suspected narco-trafficking vessels in the Caribbean and eastern Pacific, continuing the near-weekly cadence of Southern Spear operations under the coalition's operational umbrella.

events.title: US designates Brazil's PCC and Comando Vermelho as terrorist organizations; Lula rejects 'arbitrary measures'
events.detail: The US State Department designated Brazil's two largest criminal organizations, Primeiro Comando da Capital (PCC) and Comando Vermelho (CV), as Specially Designated Global Terrorists effective immediately and as Foreign Terrorist Organizations effective 5 June 2026, under Executive Order 13224. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the administration would 'continue to use all available tools' to keep illicit drugs off American streets. President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva rejected the designation, arguing it conflates profit-driven crime with ideologically motivated terrorism, warning it could damage Brazil's economy through asset freezes and restrictions on financial institutions, and saying Brazil would 'not tolerate the imposition of arbitrary measures from abroad.' Brazilian senator and 2026 presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro, Lula's leading electoral rival, had separately lobbied Trump directly for the designation. Analysts including at the Washington Post described the move as a bid to boost a Trump-aligned candidate ahead of Brazil's October 2026 election; Brazil itself remains outside the Shield of the Americas coalition.

media.caption: Brazilian President Lula da Silva rejected the US terrorist designation of PCC and Comando Vermelho as 'arbitrary measures'

events.confidenceReason: Confirmed by an official US State Department press release plus multiple corroborating Tier 2 outlets; corrects and supersedes the tracker's earlier single-source, undated account of this story.

events.title: CNN investigation questions whether boat strikes are reducing cocaine flow
events.detail: A CNN analysis of the boat-strike campaign underpinning the coalition's operations found little evidence that the strikes had meaningfully reduced cocaine trafficking volumes, suggesting traffickers may simply be adapting routes and methods rather than being deterred.

events.title: Peru becomes 18th member under President Fujimori
events.detail: Peru, under President Keiko Fujimori, formally joined the coalition in early August 2026, becoming its 18th member ahead of the second A3C ministerial forum in Panama.

era: Colombia Crisis, Panama Forum & Ground-Ops Escalation (Aug 2026)

events.title: De la Espriella sworn in, vows to join coalition on day one
events.detail: Right-wing outsider Abelardo de la Espriella was inaugurated as Colombia's president on 7 August 2026 after narrowly defeating left-wing senator Iván Cepeda in the runoff, vowing a crackdown on armed groups and confirming that Colombia would join the Shield of the Americas on his first day in office — reversing predecessor Gustavo Petro's refusal to join.

events.title: De la Espriella proposes Medellín as Colombia's coalition operations hub
events.detail: As part of a broader decentralization push, De la Espriella proposed that Colombia's participation in the coalition — coordination, liaison, and possible basing functions — be run out of Medellín rather than Bogotá.

events.title: 7.4–7.5 magnitude earthquake strikes Chocó, over 300 dead
events.detail: A major earthquake struck Colombia's Chocó department on 10 August 2026, killing at least 312 people, injuring more than 4,600, and leaving hundreds missing, with damage extending to Cali, Pereira, Quibdó, Manizales and Armenia. The disaster struck days into De la Espriella's presidency and became the backdrop for an expanded US security and assistance offer.

events.title: Trump pledges $1B security package, 'Plan Colombia 2.0'
events.detail: Following the earthquake and De la Espriella's request for expanded joint operations, Trump announced a $1 billion security assistance package for Colombia, quickly dubbed 'Plan Colombia 2.0' by observers. Sanctions imposed on outgoing president Gustavo Petro, his wife, son, and interior minister by the US Treasury's OFAC in October 2025 over alleged drug-trade links remained in force even as Washington rebuilt military cooperation with the new government.
events.confidenceReason: US and Colombian officials confirm the pledge; exact disbursement terms not yet public.

events.title: NYT, WaPo report alleged CIA covert boat-strike program off Ecuador, separate from Southern Spear
events.detail: The New York Times and Washington Post reported that a series of unclaimed attacks on three Ecuadorian fishing vessels — the Fiorella (vanished 20 Jan 2026 with eight of ten crew presumed dead), the Negra Francisca Duarte II (17 Mar 2026) and the Don Maca (26 Mar 2026) — were carried out by an unacknowledged program reported to be run by the CIA, distinct from the publicly declared Southern Spear/JTF-WHEM strike campaign this tracker otherwise follows. Survivors described English-speaking operatives wearing US flag patches, in some accounts using drones, who allegedly hooded, cuffed and tortured them before handing them to Salvadoran authorities. Reporters traced a maritime patrol aircraft — registered to a shell company with a UPS-store mailing address in Virginia, flying under a registration not listed with the FAA — from El Salvador's Ilopango airport (a former Cold War-era CIA staging base) to the vicinity of all three attacks. The Pentagon and US Coast Guard denied involvement or declined to comment. Ecuadorian prosecutor Alexandra Bravo Cedeño, who was investigating the attacks, was shot dead in Manta on 14 June 2026 in a case with no announced leads.

media.caption: Reporting traced a mystery maritime patrol aircraft to attacks on Ecuadorian fishing boats

events.confidenceReason: Based on NYT/WaPo flight-tracking, satellite reporting and survivor testimony; the Pentagon, US Coast Guard and CIA have not confirmed involvement, and no US or Ecuadorian government body has publicly attributed the attacks as of 29 Aug 2026.

events.title: Second A3C ministerial forum convenes in Panama
events.detail: Secretary of War Pete Hegseth, as A3C chairman, led the coalition's second ministerial forum in Panama on 12 August 2026, addressing defense ministers and chiefs from 18 partner nations (Argentina, Bahamas, Belize, Bolivia, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Dominican Republic, Ecuador, El Salvador, Guatemala, Guyana, Honduras, Jamaica, Panama, Paraguay, Peru, Trinidad and Tobago) on operationalizing the coalition against narco-terrorism. He met bilaterally with Panamanian President José Mulino on Panama Canal security.

events.title: Colombia formally becomes 19th coalition member
events.detail: Hegseth announced during the Panama forum that Colombia had officially joined the Shield of the Americas as its 19th member, opening the possibility of joint Colombia-US strikes against narco-terrorist groups on Colombian soil. Colombia's request for joint military operations marked the coalition's deepest operational commitment to date from a new member.
events.confidenceReason: Confirmed by US Secretary of War statement (Tier 1-adjacent Tier 2 reporting); scope of joint-operations authorization not independently confirmed as of 20 Aug 2026.

events.title: Coalition sets November deadline for A3C campaign plan
events.detail: Hegseth told the Panama forum: 'Between now and November, we are going to write an A3C campaign plan... We will staff it with our teammates and our members here in the room, and we'll approve it by November.' SOUTHCOM commander Gen. Francis Donovan said members agreed on next steps including refining priority-network campaign plans, assigning lead nations, and standing up working groups. SCHEDULED — the campaign plan has not yet been drafted or approved as of 20 August 2026.

events.title: Hegseth joins PANAMAX 2026 canal-defense exercise
events.detail: On 13 August 2026 Hegseth participated in PANAMAX 2026, SOUTHCOM's premier multinational exercise focused on collective defense of the Panama Canal, held alongside the A3C ministerial and framed as evidence of the coalition's operational reach into critical infrastructure protection.

events.title: Hegseth reaffirms 'Trump Corollary,' calls for ground attacks on cartels
events.detail: Closing the Panama forum, Hegseth explicitly reaffirmed the 'Trump Corollary' to the Monroe Doctrine and called on regional partners to escalate beyond maritime interdiction to ground operations against cartel networks, drawing criticism from regional analysts about mission creep and sovereignty concerns among member states.

events.title: SOUTHCOM activates permanent Joint Task Force Western Hemisphere
events.detail: US Southern Command commander Gen. Francis Donovan activated Joint Task Force Western Hemisphere (JTF-WHEM), a standing operational headquarters under US Marine Corps Maj. Gen. Kevin Jarrard, replacing the ad hoc Joint Task Force Southern Spear as the command's principal formation for counter-narco-terrorist operations. JTF-WHEM is designed to integrate military capabilities with the 18 A3C partner nations at the time of stand-up, ahead of Colombia's accession as the 19th member.

events.title: Donovan calls to impose 'total systemic friction' on cartel networks; read as warning to Havana
events.detail: Addressing defense officials from A3C partner nations at the Panama forum, Gen. Francis Donovan said 'we need to attack these networks, we have to apply total systemic friction against them,' asking whether the coalition was 'willing to take the fight to the enemy.' Donovan did not name Cuba, but Cuban-diaspora and regional outlets read the remarks — combined with Trump-era rhetoric and the January 2026 Venezuela precedent — as an implicit warning to Havana over alleged links between Cuban officials and drug trafficking.

media.caption: SOUTHCOM commander Gen. Francis Donovan addresses the Panama A3C forum

events.confidenceReason: Donovan's remarks did not name Cuba explicitly; SOUTHCOM has not confirmed Cuba as a specific target, so the 'warning to Havana' framing is a media interpretation rather than an official statement.

events.title: Hegseth: Colombia, Guatemala and Honduras agree to joint ground operations — Guatemala denies
events.detail: Secretary of War Pete Hegseth said Colombia, Guatemala and Honduras had agreed to allow US forces to conduct joint ground operations against cartel and 'terrorist' networks on their soil, extending the maritime Southern Spear strike campaign — which the AP tallies at more than 200 killed in over 60 boat strikes — onto land, following a similar arrangement with Ecuador launched in March 2026. Guatemalan President Bernardo Arévalo publicly denied any such agreement, saying Guatemala's constitution bars joint military operations with foreign forces and that Guatemala had only requested training, tactical planning support and intelligence sharing. Honduras and Colombia did not respond to AP's requests for comment on Hegseth's claim.

media.caption: Secretary of War Pete Hegseth speaks at the A3C forum in Panama City, 12 Aug 2026

events.confidenceReason: Guatemala's president explicitly denied the agreement on the record; Honduras and Colombia have neither confirmed nor denied Hegseth's characterization as of 21 Aug 2026.

events.title: US confirms Green Berets, Black Hawks and warships deployed to Ecuador's Esmeraldas and Manta
events.detail: Esmeraldas Governor Juan Jaramillo confirmed on the record that the US Army's 7th Special Forces Group is working alongside Ecuadorian forces against 'narcoterrorism' along the Colombian border, while Ecuadorian Defense Minister Gian Carlo Loffredo announced the arrival of three Black Hawk helicopters and two US warships at the Pacific port of Manta after meeting SOUTHCOM commander Gen. Francis Donovan there. Loffredo said the package would roughly triple Ecuador's maritime interdiction capacity along drug-trafficking routes. The deployment formalizes and expands the joint operations first launched in March 2026, predating and distinct from Hegseth's disputed 17 Aug claim about Colombia, Guatemala and Honduras. Officials did not disclose troop numbers, rules of engagement, or deployment duration; a June 2026 Ecuadorian government decree grants US military personnel 180-day visa-free entry and SOFA-style immunity from migration sanctions.

media.caption: US Black Hawk helicopters and warships stationed at Manta, Ecuador, Aug 2026

events.confidenceReason: Confirmed on the record by both Ecuador's Esmeraldas governor and Defense Minister, alongside SOUTHCOM's commander; corroborated by two independent Tier 2 outlets.

events.title: JTF-WHEM's first strike ends two-month pause on boat strikes, killing 2
events.detail: Under Gen. Francis Donovan's direction, the newly activated Joint Task Force Western Hemisphere carried out its first lethal kinetic strike on a low-profile vessel — described in SOUTHCOM's video as a semi-submersible 'narco sub' — in the eastern Pacific, killing 2 people. It was the first Southern Spear-lineage strike since 21 June 2026, a roughly two-month pause, and brings the campaign's confirmed total to over 67 vessels destroyed and 200+ killed since September 2025. SOUTHCOM said the strike showed the task force could 'accelerate, synchronize and execute lethal actions' against narco-terrorist networks. Sen. Tim Kaine had urged the White House earlier in August to halt what he called an 'illegal, costly and ineffective' campaign, citing classified information that strikes had likely killed people not involved in trafficking; the Pentagon Inspector General is separately reviewing whether standard targeting procedures were followed.

media.caption: SOUTHCOM video screenshot of the strike on a suspected narco-trafficking vessel in the eastern Pacific

events.confidenceReason: SOUTHCOM confirms the strike, casualty count and vessel type via video and statement; independent verification of the vessel's cargo/intent is not possible, and a Pentagon IG review of targeting procedures is ongoing.

events.title: Second strike in three days kills 4 in Caribbean, toll passes 227
events.detail: Joint Task Force Western Hemisphere struck a suspected go-fast drug-smuggling vessel in the Caribbean Sea on 25 August 2026, killing 4 people — the second lethal strike in three days after the roughly two-month operational pause ended with the 23 August Pacific strike. Gen. Francis Donovan said JTF-WHEM would continue to 'hunt, disrupt, and defeat' narco-terrorist networks. The strike brought the campaign's confirmed toll to at least 227 killed across 68 strikes since September 2025. It came days after Sen. Tim Kaine wrote to President Trump that a review of classified intelligence showed the campaign has likely killed people not involved in narcotrafficking, calling them 'murder victims,' as the Pentagon Inspector General's review of targeting procedures continues.

media.caption: SOUTHCOM video screenshot of the vessel in the Caribbean Sea before the 25 August strike

events.confidenceReason: SOUTHCOM confirms the strike and casualty count via video and statement; independent verification of the vessel's cargo/intent is not possible, consistent with the ongoing Pentagon IG review of targeting procedures.

events.title: JTF-WHEM boards and sinks Treasury-sanctioned narco 'refueling station' vessel with Ecuador
events.detail: Acting on Gen. Francis Donovan's orders and in coordination with the Government of Ecuador, Joint Task Force Western Hemisphere launched Marines and Sailors from USS San Antonio (LPD-17) to interdict a Treasury-sanctioned vessel operating as a floating refueling station for the Los Choneros narco-terrorist network in international waters of the eastern Pacific. The boarding team searched and cleared the vessel without incident; the people aboard were safely escorted to Ecuador, and US forces then sank the empty vessel. SOUTHCOM described the interdiction — a non-lethal boarding rather than a kinetic strike — as disrupting the logistics chain that lets smuggling boats operate far from shore.

media.caption: US Marines and Sailors from USS San Antonio board the sanctioned refueling vessel

events.confidenceReason: Confirmed by SOUTHCOM official statement and video; no independent dispute of the facts as of 29 Aug 2026.

events.title: Flávio Bolsonaro meets Bukele's justice minister, pledges to declare cartels terrorist groups if elected
events.detail: Brazilian senator and leading 2026 presidential candidate Flávio Bolsonaro met El Salvador's Minister of Justice and Public Security, Gustavo Villatoro, in São Paulo on 30 August 2026, ahead of Brazil's October election against President Lula. Bolsonaro said he left the meeting 'inspired' and pledged that, if elected, he would harden criminal legislation, declare organizations including the PCC and Comando Vermelho — already designated Specially Designated Global Terrorists by Washington in May 2026 — domestic terrorist groups, create a dedicated federal public security ministry, and build roughly 500,000 new prison spaces including five new federal prisons. He cited El Salvador's mano dura crackdown under coalition founding member Nayib Bukele as a model, citing a claimed 97% homicide reduction since 2018, without addressing Human Rights Watch allegations of mass arbitrary detention, torture and deaths in custody under El Salvador's ongoing state of exception. Bolsonaro's platform aligns with the Shield of the Americas coalition's hardline framing even though Brazil itself remains a coalition holdout.

media.caption: Flávio Bolsonaro pledged to declare Brazilian gangs terrorist organizations if elected president

events.confidenceReason: Corroborated by two independent Tier 2 outlets (English and Portuguese-language) reporting the same on-record meeting and pledge.

events.title: SOUTHCOM's Donovan opens two-day Colombia tour, weighs aircraft rehab and joint tactical agenda
events.detail: Gen. Francis Donovan landed in Bogotá on 26 August 2026 for a two-day visit — the first senior SOUTHCOM visit under President Abelardo de la Espriella's administration — touring the Pacific port of Tumaco (Nariño department, a major coca-cultivation and semi-submersible/fast-boat departure zone) and the Tolemaida military base, the Colombian army's main aviation and training hub. Technical discussions covered intelligence-sharing, reconnaissance and special-operations coordination; no formal written agreement was released. Follow-up reporting in the days after described the visit as formalizing a 'joint tactical agenda' between Donovan and De la Espriella, including rehabilitating Colombia's grounded aircraft fleet — 11 of the army's 19 Soviet-era Mi-17 helicopters were left non-operational by the change of government. The visit followed Washington's 7 August announcement of the $1B 'Plan Colombia 2.0' package, even as Colombia remained on the State Department's list of countries judged to have 'failed demonstrably' on drug control under a September 2025 determination.

media.caption: Gen. Francis L. Donovan, commander of US Southern Command

events.confidenceReason: Visit and itinerary confirmed by an on-the-ground Tier 2 report the day after; the 'joint tactical agenda' and aircraft-rehab specifics come from later follow-up reporting rather than an official joint statement.

events.title: SOUTHCOM, Ecuador and Colombia weigh binational border base against traffickers
events.detail: At a high-level meeting spanning Tumaco (Colombia's Nariño department) and San Lorenzo (Ecuador's Esmeraldas province) on 27-28 August 2026, Gen. Francis Donovan met Ecuadorian Defense Minister Gian Carlo Loffredo and Colombian military and government officials to weigh an unprecedented binational military base on the two countries' shared border, aimed at pressuring trafficking networks including FARC dissidents and the ELN active across Nariño, Putumayo, Esmeraldas, Carchi and Sucumbíos. No location, command structure, personnel numbers or timeline were announced, and the proposal runs up against Ecuador's constitutional prohibition on foreign military bases — the same provision at issue in the ongoing dispute over the Esmeraldas/Manta special-forces deployment. The three sides agreed to deepen intelligence-sharing and coordinate leadership-targeting operations regardless of the base's fate.

media.caption: Officials from the US, Ecuador and Colombia discuss a proposed binational border base

events.confidenceReason: Confirmed by two independent Tier 2 outlets (Argentine and Ecuadorian) describing the same meeting; no formal decision or joint statement has been published.

events.title: One year after the first strike, HRW and investigative reporting tally 227 dead, only 26 named
events.detail: Marking one year since the campaign's first strike on 2 September 2025, Human Rights Watch published 'United States: Year of Extrajudicial Killings at Sea,' and The Intercept, Democracy Now! and other outlets published anniversary investigations into the boat-strike campaign that has become the coalition's operational backbone. The reports tally at least 69 strikes and 227 people killed, including roughly 28 identified survivors of whom only 3 were rescued alive; just 26 of 227 victims (about 11%) have been publicly named, spanning Venezuelan, Mexican, Colombian, Ecuadorian, Trinidadian and Saint Lucian nationals, and none has been formally charged with a crime. HRW highlighted a lawsuit filed 27 January 2026 by relatives of two named Trinidadian victims, Rishi Samaroo and Chad Joseph, with ACLU and Center for Constitutional Rights support, seeking compensation from the US government. HRW's Ida Sawyer said the administration 'has summarily killed more than 200 people over the past year, bragging about these killings online and facing no accountability.' The Pentagon maintains the strikes are lawful actions against narco-terrorist threats; no independent judicial review of individual strikes has been published.

media.caption: Pentagon-released image of a suspected drug-smuggling vessel prior to a 2025 Southern Spear strike

events.confidenceReason: Strike/casualty tallies and the named-victim/survivor breakdown are corroborated across three independent investigative and NGO sources; the 'extrajudicial killing' legal characterization remains contested by the Pentagon, consistent with the tracker's existing legality claim.

events.title: JTF-WHEM sinks second Los Choneros-linked 'floating refueling station' off Ecuador
events.detail: At the direction of SOUTHCOM Commander Gen. Francis L. Donovan and in coordination with the Government of Ecuador, JTF-WHEM boarded, searched and sank a vessel operating as a floating refueling station in international waters in the Eastern Pacific on 2 September 2026 — the second such non-lethal interdiction in a week, following a 28 August 2026 operation. SOUTHCOM said the vessel supported at-sea drug trafficking linked to the Ecuadorian criminal group Los Choneros. Marines and sailors boarded and cleared the vessel without incident before sinking it and turning the crew over to Ecuadorian authorities; no casualties were reported. Donovan said the interdiction 'cuts off a critical node in the traffickers' logistics chain.' The operation extends a pause in lethal strikes that has held since JTF-WHEM's 25 August strike, even as families of missing Ecuadorian fishermen continue to seek answers about earlier, unrelated attacks alleged to be part of a separate covert CIA program.

media.caption: Video showed armed personnel boarding the floating refueling station before it was sunk

events.confidenceReason: Confirmed by an official SOUTHCOM press release naming the commander, vessel type and linked cartel, corroborated by CBS News.

events.title: PoderData poll shows Flávio Bolsonaro edging ahead of Lula for the first time since May
events.detail: A PoderData/Aya survey of 3,000 voters across all 27 states (fieldwork 30 August–2 September 2026, published 3 September) put Flávio Bolsonaro ahead of President Lula 45%–44% in a simulated runoff — within the poll's ±1.8-point margin of error, but the first time PoderData has shown Bolsonaro numerically ahead since May, after Lula had led by one point a week earlier. State-level numbers show a starkly divided electorate: Bolsonaro leads in São Paulo (46.8%–43.3%), Mato Grosso (52%–37%) and Espírito Santo (48%–42%), while Lula dominates the northeast, including Bahia (58.1%–29%) and Pernambuco (59%–35%). The result lands a day after a separate Quaest/Globo poll showed the race at a statistical tie (42%–41%), adding to a run of tightening surveys ahead of Brazil's 4 October first round. Brazil remains outside the Shield of the Americas coalition; Bolsonaro's campaign is the most visible domestic constituency for the coalition's hardline, terrorist-designation framing of Brazilian gangs.

media.caption: Flávio Bolsonaro and President Lula are locked in a tightening race ahead of Brazil's October election

events.confidenceReason: Poll topline and state-level breakdown corroborated by the polling firm's original Brazilian-market coverage (CNN Brasil) and the Rio Times' English-language report of the same survey; a single-firm lead within the margin of error, so framed as a tightening race rather than a decisive shift.

events.title: JTF-WHEM sinks third Los Choneros-linked 'floating refueling station' off Ecuador
events.detail: At the direction of SOUTHCOM Commander Gen. Francis L. Donovan and in coordination with the Government of Ecuador, Littoral Combat Force-24 launched from USS San Antonio (LPD-17) and interdicted a vessel operating as a floating refueling station for the Los Choneros narco-terrorist organization in international waters of the Eastern Pacific on 3 September 2026 — the third such non-lethal interdiction since 28 August and the second in 24 hours. An MH-60 Seahawk helicopter provided airborne tracking, FLIR surveillance and sniper overwatch while boarding teams in rigid-hull inflatable boats searched and cleared the vessel without incident; the individuals aboard were transferred to Ecuadorian authorities before US forces scuttled the vessel. No casualties were reported, extending the pause in lethal strikes that has held since JTF-WHEM's 25 August strike.

media.caption: The intercepted Los Choneros-linked refueling vessel in the Eastern Pacific

events.confidenceReason: Confirmed by an official SOUTHCOM press release naming the commander, unit and linked cartel, corroborated by The Epoch Times.

events.title: JTF-WHEM sinks fourth, multi-vessel Los Choneros-linked 'floating refueling station' off Ecuador
events.detail: On 5 September 2026, at the direction of SOUTHCOM, JTF-WHEM forces interdicted a multi-vessel floating refueling station — a main vessel with attached support vessels — supporting Los Choneros drug-trafficking operations in international waters of the Eastern Pacific. Forces from USS San Antonio again combined MH-60 Seahawk overwatch with rigid-hull inflatable boarding craft; individuals removed from the main vessel were transferred to Ecuadorian authorities, after which US forces sank the main vessel and its attached support vessels. It was the fourth such non-lethal refueling-station interdiction since 28 August and the third in a single week, with lethal strikes still paused since 25 August.

media.caption: US forces sink the multi-vessel Los Choneros refueling station in the Eastern Pacific

events.confidenceReason: Confirmed by an official SOUTHCOM press release naming the vessel type, unit and linked cartel, corroborated by Fox News.
